cards.title: Bioanalytical Context and Assay Validity
cards.claim: Reported concentrations depend on a defined assay with specific calibration ranges, LLOQ, and stability profiles. QC acceptance criteria (e.g., ±15% of nominal) and stability tests (freeze-thaw, bench-top) validate the data's reliability. Endogenous analytes require specific QC handling (spiked vs. unspiked) to ensure accuracy.
conditions: Applies when evaluating the quality and traceability of concentration data.
Requires knowledge of the assay method (e.g., LC-MS/MS) and matrix-specific validation.
Stability and recovery data must be available to interpret concentration changes over time.
required_inputs: Provenance: Reference to specific validation guidelines (e.g., ICH M10) or study-specific validation reports.
Identity: Assay method name and specific analyte measured.
Prerequisites: Documented LLOQ, ULOQ, and stability conditions (temperature, pH, time).
Missing-input gates: If assay validation details are absent, quantitative-reuse qualification is marked as unresolved; this does not establish invalid data or failed validation.
limitations: A source-reported result is not a new fitted result.
PDF text extraction does not validate table layout or figure accuracy.
Assay limitations (e.g., interference) must be retained in annotations.
cards.downstream_use: Informs whether assay evidence supports quantitative reuse for NCA or compartmental modeling. If stability or selectivity documentation is absent, mark qualification as unresolved and flag dependent reuse for review; absence of documentation alone does not establish invalid data or failed validation.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Dose/event/time, analyte, matrix, units and free/total concentration definitions attached to descriptive evidence

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
